title: THESE JARS ARE DANGEROUS
text: THESE JARS ARE DANGEROUS. THESE JARS ARE DANGEROUS! Ptomaine or botulism poisoning looking for a place to happen. I've been canning and making jam for over 50 years. I know what to do. Since writing this review a bunch more of the jars have come unsealed. Actually most of them so far. I did not have room in my freezer for all of the jam as I wasn't planning on freezing it. What a waste of time, money and labor! I bought three boxes of these & left a good review after I opened the first box & was impressed with the extras: little chalkboard kitty labels, a white marker pen & 6 extra lids & bands. I thought they were a good deal. But here's a catchy little poem for ya---It's not a good deal if the lids don't seal. I made 27 jars of blackberry jam & we're talking pricey jam as the berries were $50 for two gallons. Of those 27 jars so far, 7 are duds and I had to put them in the freezer because either they never sealed to begin with or they sealed and then popped up and came unsealed. I won't be using the remainder of the three boxes except for freezer jam which I could use plastic containers for much cheaper. Sticking with Ball or Mason. Saving a few bucks isn't worth risking making my family sick or worse.
